operators.description: Load region table, find r_regionkey where r_name='AMERICA'

Load nation table. Build two structures: (1) america_custkey_nations: bitset of n_nationkey where n_regionkey=america_regionkey (for customer-side filter), (2) nation_name_lookup: direct array[25] of n_name indexed by n_nationkey (for supplier-side n2 name lookup)

america_custkey_nations.description: n_nationkey values where n_regionkey = america_regionkey (AMERICA region nations)

nation_name_lookup.description: n_name string indexed by n_nationkey, for looking up supplier's nation (n2)

brazil_nationkey.description: n_nationkey where n_name = 'BRAZIL', for conditional aggregation

operators.description: Scan hash_part_by_partkey (dense array), build bitset of p_partkey where p_type = 'ECONOMY ANODIZED STEEL'
operators.notes: ~150 distinct p_type values, uniform distribution → ~13.3K matching parts. Bitset is 244KB, fits comfortably in L3 cache.

operators.description: Main processing pipeline executed inside scan_lineitem_full callback. For each lineitem row, apply cascading filters and accumulate into thread-local aggregates.

substeps.notes: Most selective filter — applied first. Single bit test, ~0.3ns per row.

substeps.description: Lookup orders via dense_pk on l_orderkey to get o_orderdate and o_custkey
substeps.notes: O(1) array lookup. orders_pk_idx maps o_orderkey -> row_id, then index into materialized o_orderdate[] and o_custkey[] arrays.
2 years out of ~7 year range in orders table.

substeps.description: Lookup customer via dense_pk on o_custkey to get c_nationkey
Filter c_nationkey IN america_custkey_nations (AMERICA region nations via n1→region path)
substeps.notes: 5 regions with roughly equal nations → 20% pass rate.

substeps.description: Lookup supplier via dense_pk on l_suppkey to get s_nationkey
Compute o_year, volume, and conditionally aggregate into thread-local accumulators

operators.description: Thread-local aggregation during callback, then merge across threads

aggregates.name: brazil_volume
aggregates.expression: SUM(CASE WHEN s_nationkey = brazil_nationkey THEN volume ELSE 0 END)

thread_local.description: 2 years × 2 accumulators (brazil_volume, total_volume). 32 bytes per thread — trivially fits in registers.
thread_local.merge: element-wise sum across all thread-local arrays

operators.description: Compute mkt_share = brazil_volume / total_volume for each year
Output sorted by o_year ascending, project (o_year, mkt_share)
operators.notes: Only 2 rows (1995, 1996) — sort is trivial, just emit in order.

join_order.notes: Most selective join — applied first. Bitset on p_partkey (244KB, L3-resident). Single bit test per lineitem row.
O(1) array lookup via orders_pk_idx. Date filter applied as residual after lookup.
O(1) custkey→c_nationkey lookup, then bitset test for AMERICA region nations.
O(1) suppkey→s_nationkey lookup. All suppliers match (no filter on supplier), just need nation key for n2 name.

parallelism.scope: callback from scan_lineitem_full — parallelism is inherited from shared scan's morsel partitioning
parallelism.thread_local_state: double[2][2] per thread (32 bytes), no contention
parallelism.merge: single-threaded element-wise sum of thread-local arrays after callback completes

indexes.purpose: Pre-build part_filter_bitset by scanning p_type column
Direct array access for nation dimension

notes: Q8 is a 8-table join but most complexity is absorbed by shared components and dense_pk indexes. The critical optimization is applying the highly selective part filter (0.67%) first as a bitset semi-join on the streaming lineitem callback, reducing 60M rows to ~400K before any random-access lookups. All subsequent joins are O(1) dense_pk array lookups. The final aggregation has only 2 groups (years 1995-1996) and fits in registers. Total random-access lookups: ~400K orders + ~114K customer + ~22.8K supplier ≈ 537K, all into memory-resident arrays.
